disclaimer: All surplus, attendance, driver, offer, acceptance, and delivery events are synthetic. Institution schedule geometry does not imply participation or affiliation.

bakedboston_mip.label: BakedBoston Gurobi MIP
bakedboston_mip.description: Maximizes expected completed assignments first, then the normalized food, fairness, environmental, and driver-fit objective across simultaneous drivers.
bakedboston_mip.selectionDescription: The driver chooses recommendation rank 1, the highest-scoring route in the conflict-free menu produced after the joint assignment.
bakedboston_mip.objective: Maximize expected completed pickups, then the normalized food, fairness, environmental, and driver-fit score within 1% of that optimum.
inputsUsed: hard search horizon and facility windows

nair_2018_distance_first.label: Nair et al. distance-first adaptation
nair_2018_distance_first.description: A minimal volunteer-route adaptation of the 2018 periodic unpaired pickup-and-delivery model: protect service first, then minimize miles.
nair_2018_distance_first.selectionDescription: The model assigns one route to a driver; that assigned route is recorded as the driver's selection.
nair_2018_distance_first.objective: Maximize assigned food-ready pickups, then minimize total route distance.
inputsUsed: current driver location as route origin

xue_zou_2025_total_curb.label: Xue–Zou Total-Curb adaptation
xue_zou_2025_total_curb.description: A minimal volunteer-route adaptation of the 2025 Total-Curb model: protect service first, then minimize total direct system CO2e.
xue_zou_2025_total_curb.selectionDescription: The model assigns one route to a driver; that assigned route is recorded as the driver's selection.
xue_zou_2025_total_curb.objective: Maximize assigned food-ready pickups, then minimize uncollected waste, selected-route residual waste, and transportation CO2e.
inputsUsed: current driver location as route origin
route distance and fixed direct-emissions coefficients

horner_2021_slsf_noz.label: Horner et al. stochastic-menu adaptation
horner_2021_slsf_noz.description: A minimal adaptation of the 2021 SLSF-noZ model: optimize short personalized menus over seeded stochastic willingness scenarios, then assign among routes drivers are willing to fulfill.
horner_2021_slsf_noz.selectionDescription: The driver signals willingness for any acceptable menu options; the platform's recourse solve assigns one willing route, which is recorded as the driver's selection.
horner_2021_slsf_noz.objective: Maximize expected completed food-ready pickups over 100 seeded willingness scenarios, then minimize expected route distance as a tie-break.
inputsUsed: current driver location as route origin
route distance as an exact-service tie-break
inputsExcluded: food quantity and pantry distribution as objectives

random_feasible.label: Random feasible
random_feasible.description: Chooses randomly from routes that satisfy the same timing constraints.

shortest_route.label: Shortest route
shortest_route.description: Greedily chooses the smallest driving-time burden.

earliest_deadline.label: Earliest deadline
earliest_deadline.description: Greedily serves bakery pickup deadlines that occur soonest.

highest_priority.label: Highest pantry priority
highest_priority.description: Greedily favors pantries with the greatest current priority.

driver_fit.label: Driver destination fit
driver_fit.description: Greedily minimizes deviation from each driver's preferred destination.

environmentalAssumptions.interpretation: Declared academic scenario coefficients. The primary objective credits the difference between the bakery's no-pickup waste outcome and the waste remaining after Q × usability × pantry distribution, then subtracts tonne-kilometre transport emissions. Avoided production is held at zero in the primary score.

selectionRule: The joint Gurobi solve first maximizes expected completed distinct bakery pickups. Within one percent of that optimum it maximizes a normalized 100-point score: pantry coverage (10), raw donation volume (10), raw donation evenness (10), ultimately saved food volume (10), saved-food evenness (10), historical pantry opportunity priority (10), net direct CO2 benefit (20), and driver fit (20).

recommendationAllocation.zeroRecommendationRule: A driver receives no recommendation only when there are fewer distinct feasible bakery pickups than simultaneous drivers or that driver has no time-feasible route.

metricMethodology.actualSelection: For BakedBoston's route-choice menu, the simulated driver selects rank 1, the highest-scoring route. The Horner adaptation instead follows its source formulation: drivers signal willingness for menu options and the platform makes the final recourse assignment. For other direct-assignment models, the assigned route is recorded as the driver's selection.
metricMethodology.acceptanceModel: Expected acceptance and likely-rejection measures are prediction-based diagnostics; they do not override the deterministic recorded selection used in this demonstration.
metricMethodology.comparison: All models share the exact same seeded surplus, daily food and usability draws, pantry openings and distribution fractions, waste allocations, driver events, facility windows, and feasible route geometry. Each selector reads only the inputs represented in its formulation; every result is then evaluated through the same food, environmental, travel, and acceptance ledger.

totalImpactMethodology.label: Balanced Total Impact
totalImpactMethodology.description: A post-hoc communication index that gives equal weight to six non-duplicated outcome pillars. Each pillar is scored from 0 to 100 relative to the best policy in this exact scenario.

service.label: Completed service
service.description: Completed bakery-to-pantry deliveries in the realized routing-capacity replay.

food.label: Food recovery
food.description: Ultimately distributed food using Q × bakery usability × pantry distribution.

environment.label: Environmental benefit
environment.description: Net direct waste-pathway benefit after subtracting transportation CO2e.

equity.label: Distribution equity
equity.description: Equal average of pantry coverage, raw-donation equality, and saved-food equality.

volunteer.label: Volunteer fit
volunteer.description: Mean modeled route-acceptance probability, which combines driving and requested time/location fit.

efficiency.label: Route efficiency
efficiency.description: Average route-distance efficiency relative to the shortest-distance policy in the same scenario.

totalImpactMethodology.caveat: This scenario-relative index is not used by any optimizer, is not an externally validated social-impact measure, and can change when the scenario or comparison set changes. The underlying physical and fairness metrics remain the auditable result.
